Newborn bleeding on day 3, no vitamin K at birth, breastfed → Haemorrhagic disease of the newborn
12-month-old on whole cow's milk since 6 months, pale → Iron deficiency anaemia
f: Breastfeed within 1 hour · exclusive to 6 months · complementary food from 6 months · continue to 2 years or more
Chin touches the breast · mouth wide open · lower lip turned out · more areola above than below
Best sign: adequate weight gain · ≥ 6 wet nappies a day · ≥ 8 feeds in 24 hours
Colostrum: more IgA and protein · hindmilk: more fat · low in vitamin K and D · lactoferrin binds iron (bacteriostatic)
Infant with galactosaemia · mother on chemotherapy or radioactive drugs · (HIV: breastfeed on ART as per national policy)
150 ml/kg/day · cow's milk protein allergy: extensively hydrolysed formula · no whole cow's milk or honey before 1 year
trap: Active TB in the mother is not a reason to stop: breastfeed, give the baby isoniazid · goat's milk → folate/B12 deficiency · concentrated formula → hypernatraemic dehydration · honey → botulism
